options.title: Why Does the Paris Metro Run on Rubber Tyres?
options.first_line: This Paris Metro train runs on rubber tyres, like a truck. So what keeps it on the track?
options.first_frame: A blue Paris Metro train roaring out of a dark tunnel toward the camera, a cutaway under it showing fat rubber tyres spinning on a flat track.

options.title: The Paris Metro Train Hiding Two Sets of Wheels
options.first_line: Under this Paris Metro train, there's a second set of wheels that almost never touches anything.
options.first_frame: A Paris Metro bogie sliced open in 3D, the rubber tyre spinning while a steel wheel just behind it glows, hovering a finger's width above an ordinary rail.

options.title: Rubber Tyres vs Steel Rails: Why Paris Picked Both
options.first_line: Most trains roll steel on steel. Paris put some of its Metro on rubber, and kept the steel anyway.
options.first_frame: Split screen: a steel train wheel on a rail on the left, a rubber tyre on a flat concrete track on the right, both spinning, a Paris Metro sign above.

why: A rubber-tyred train you can picture roaring at you raises a real how-is-that-possible question (what keeps it on the track?) that neither the title nor the first line answers, while B already gives away the hidden steel wheels and C's title states the answer.
